P.h: North Korea's PolinRider force-pushes malware into 7,600+ GitHub repos
P.p: Stolen GitHub tokens let the campaign rewrite commits developers already made. Loaders hide after hundreds of spaces in build configs, conftest.py or VS Code auto-run tasks, so building the project or just opening the folder runs them. The C2 address is read from Ethereum wallet transactions, so server takedowns do nothing.
P.s: Block outbound traffic to 95.135.181[.]84 and 103.179.142[.]155. Check conftest.py, utils packages and .vscode/tasks.json for unexpected code, and rotate GitHub tokens if you find any. Related activity traces back to February 2025.

items.h: Hex.pm servers hit by remote code execution
items.d: Unauthenticated Erlang-term bodies ran code on six web servers via a gadget chain. Patched in 20 minutes, no tampered packages found, but email, password hashes and 2FA secrets can't be ruled out. Reset password and 2FA; upgrade Ash to 3.38.0.

items.h: Rotate AWS keys stored in easyDNS control panel
items.d: easyDNS urges every user storing AWS keys for Route53 integration to rotate them immediately after reports of key compromises (TLDR IT).

items.h: Zero-permission app roots Samsung Galaxy S23 and S26
items.d: DualDAR relayAsync chain ends in kernel read/write and SELinux off. Fixed in the August and September 2026 updates. Require September patch level via MDM.

P.h: AI coding agent found a financial firm's access key in under six minutes
P.p: An attacker used OpenCode, Chrome and curl. The agent read a decoy API document, followed a link to a fake environment, found a planted key and tested it. Jesta contained it, and the intruder stopped after five minutes 44 seconds. The address was in no threat feed, so blocklists would have missed it.
P.s: Behavioral signals worked: a desktop browser claiming to be a phone, rapid key attempts, and a link that existed only in the API docs. TLDR DevOps adds Teleport's advice: agents start with no access, request only what a task needs, and leave an audit trail.

tiles.t: US Treasury subdomains taken over for $3 each
tiles.d: Intruder claimed dangling AWS Elastic IPs, including five treasury.gov hosts. AWS says it has no plans to change its approach.

P.h: Chainguard moves thousands of daily builds off GitHub Actions
P.p: To stop release queues stalling during cloud outages, Chainguard runs builds on its own microVM infrastructure. Its CVE-remediation agents now succeed 97 to 98 percent of the time each week, and package bumps auto-merge about 99 percent of the time.
P.s: Also new: HashiCorp made HCL-based tfpolicy for Terraform Stacks generally available, plus SCIM 2.0 provisioning for HCP Terraform and agent-ready CLI commands with JSON output.

items.h: Nvidia pauses server shipments to Southeast Asia
items.d: Dell and Super Micro told to hold shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia while export compliance is checked. A rule restricting remote chip access by Chinese firms drives it.
